subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should gateway operator scopes become an input to agent runtime tool authorization through a supported toolsByScope-style policy layer?
rationale: This would define a new authorization/config boundary across gateway auth, session identity, and agent tool filtering, and current docs intentionally limit operator scopes to a trusted operator domain.

options.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve a narrow operator-scope policy contract with precedence, docs, tests, and explicit threat-model language before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Session/Sender Surfaces
options.body: Decline toolsByScope and document sender/group policy, session envelopes, and conversation identity as the supported tool-restriction paths.

options.title: Fold Into Tenant RBAC
options.body: Treat this as a subproblem of the broader multi-tenant RBAC FRD and defer scope-to-tool behavior until tenant-scoped scopes are designed.

recommendation.title: Design Scope-Aware Tool Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve a narrow operator-scope policy contract with precedence, docs, tests, and explicit threat-model language before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the scoped conversation profile and gateway/tool-policy security boundary.
